the synthesis, characterization, and electrochemical properties of selenocynate containing transition metal (M) chalcogenides (Se, M = Fe, Co, Ni) supported by N doped carbon materials (denoted as FeSe/CN, CoSe/CNC, NiSe/CN, respectively).
the preparation of a transition metal selenocyanide catalyst and its use as an oxygen reduction reaction catalyst.

the synthesis, characterization, and catalytic performance of a selenocyanated transition metal chalcogene supported by nitrogen densed carbon materials (CoSe/CN) as the cathode electro-catalyst for alkaline membrane fuel cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the selenocyanato containing transition metal chalenide (SeCN-M) catalysts have been synthesized, and their catalytic activity for the ORR has been evaluated.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new class of catalyst that can be used as the oxygen reduction reaction ( ORR) catalyst for fuel cells.
the selenocyanato containing transition metal chelocgenides supported by nitrogen-doped carbon materials, such as CoSe/CNs, are excellent electrocatalysts for oxygen reduction reactions (ORRs).
the selenocyanato containing transition metal chalconides supported by nitrogen-doped carbon materials are promising catalysts for the oxygen reduction reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ORR activity of CoSe/CNs was significantly enhanced by SeCN, which is an important factor in improving ORR activity.

the presence of SeCN bonding in the CoSe/CN catalyst promotes the ORR by facilitating electron transfer and the presence of the N doped carbon support enhances the catalytic performance by increasing the reaction kinetics of the ORR.
CoSe/CN can be a promising catalyst for the ORR.
